i normally never really leave reviews for games, but this one has enamored me so much that it would be a crime not to. i originally saw a video about the demo online (shout-out cozy tea games) and was drawn in by the gorgeous and adorable art style, but what really made me fall in love with it is the writing. i love visual novels, and this has everything of a perfect one-- a story with depth, lovable characters, and deep world building that im so eager to dive head-first into once the full game releases. i love how we're able to follow the lives of every character through our conversations with them, social media posts, and (presumedly) their repeated visits to the salon, and im so excited to see how their stories intersect with each other and impact starfish city (i NEED to see what happens with lumi and aki!! i hope they become friends!!). i also love the hints at freddie's backstory and what happened with her old coworker, im looking forward to seeing how that and the stuff with edi plays out!

the gameplay is also very fun :D the haircutting bits remind me of hair salon games i used to play growing up. its a fun challenge to figure out what each client wants, but its easy enough where it doesn't completely stress me out. as other comments have said, itd be nice if more parts of the haircutting process were interactive, or if there was more than one interactive element per client.

something else id really like to see is more of starfish city/the hair salon, or even just more short scenes in between the haircuts to break up the flow and keep things from feeling repetitive. i loved the lunch break with nella, and i wish it was longer!! like it would be cool to watch luca and varo debate on tv, or to watch one of nella's fights! some more interactions on the phone would be nice as well, like if we could look at user profiles or make our own posts.

this game is so nice to just sit back and relax to while playing :) hats off to the artists, the writers, and the programmers for creating such a lovely game. im looking forward to seeing the rest of what starfish city has to offer!! <3 (PS. plz let us date the demon, k thx)

I think this game is a conceptual strike of genius. Using a hair salon as a setting for a Coffee Talk style game makes perfect sense and the beastfolk aspect is a very natural way of adding a fun spin on the hairdressing as well as being an avenue for the topics the game is addressing in it's dialogue. 

The amount of cohesion both thematically and in audio-visual presentation is impressive. This demo really relaxes you into the world and it's characters without an overly-explicit bit of info-dumping or exposition; it's all communicated through the conversational style of story telling the game has commited itself to. 

Every customer feels distinct in their writing which is further emphasised by the music (which sounds great) changing for each character and the expressive art thats's been designed for them. Every part of this demo is a delight to listen to and look at.

I'm not typically fond of social media aspects in games but the phone segment at the end of the day is used quite tastefully giving the player extra tidbits of information on the so-far established characters and small insights into the world the game is set in.

A really great foundation has been set here and I'm looking forward to seeing how it builds on that in the full release.
